items.prompt: Which national leader is also known as the 'Father of the Nation'?
What was Mahatma Gandhi's full name?
What is the name of the women's army unit formed by Subhash Chandra Bose?

items.question: When and where was Mahatma Gandhi born? What did he study in England?
items.answer: Mahatma Gandhi was born on 2nd October, 1869, in Porbandar, Gujarat. He studied law in England.

items.question: Which slogan was given by Lokmanya Tilak to encourage millions of Indians?
items.answer: "Swaraj is my birthright and I shall have it."

items.question: Which two slogans were used by Netaji to encourage the Indians?
items.answer: "Jai Hind" and "Give me blood, I will give you freedom."

items.question: What were the two methods used by Mahatma Gandhi to fight against the British?
Write three sentences on Sardar Patel.
items.answer: Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel was a lawyer by profession. He was a strong and brave leader. He was inspired by Mahatma Gandhi to take part in the struggle for freedom. He is also known as the 'Iron Man of India'.

items.question: Why did Rani Laxmibai fight against the British?
items.answer: Rani Laxmibai fought against the British because she wanted to save her kingdom from the British. She joined the soldiers from Meerut and fought for Jhansi. She, along with other leaders, fought against the British in the Revolt of 1857.

items.question: Great people never give up in spite of difficulties. What do you do when you face difficulties in your studies?
items.answer: When I face difficulties in my studies, I never give up. I try again and again. I take help from my teacher and parents. I practice more and more until I understand well.

items.question: Mahatma Gandhi was a messenger of peace. What can you learn from him as a leader?
items.answer: I can learn to always speak the truth and be honest. I can solve problems in a peaceful way without fighting. I can be kind and helpful to others and respect everyone equally. I can also learn to stand up for what is right and work hard for the welfare of the people.
